title: Which square tile should {{NAME_1}} buy for the room?
description: A new house has a bare main room, twelve feet by sixteen feet. A photo opens the video, then a drawn plan and a row of square tiles of different sizes. The video stops on one open question about the tile size, with no answer shown.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square tile fits a room only when its side fills both walls exactly. Ask each child to guess a size and a reason, and do not confirm or reject any guess. Watch for children who pick a size by looking at one wall only.

source: A room to cover with square tiles
video_script.why: Before any word of factors, the child meets the real question: which square tile fits a rectangular floor exactly, using the fewest tiles.
video_script.substitution: Picture the floor as a rectangle and each tile as a square that must lie edge to edge with no cutting.
video_script.anchor: The new main room of the book's house, twelve feet by sixteen feet, to be covered with square tiles.

names.{{NAME_1}}: builds a new house and tiles the main room (12 ft by 16 ft)

never_show: any tile size that fits, with a tick
a tile that leaves a gap, labelled with its size
maths_rules: The main room is a rectangle 12 ft by 16 ft.
The tiles are squares laid edge to edge with no tile cut, and the side is a whole number of feet.
The row of tiles is drawn without numbers; no size is called fitting or not fitting.
The open question: which size to buy so that the fewest tiles cover the floor. The answer is never shown or hinted.
video_script.design: One idea: a tile fits only when it fills both walls exactly. Assumes nothing. The photo sits as a dimmed backdrop in the first beat and fades before the drawn plan arrives; the plan stays to the end.
